<!--lint ignore no-emphasis-as-heading-->
> **Why this list exists**
>
> Too much of the software we depend on has turned into a toll booth. Tools you used to buy once are now monthly rentals. Features you already had move behind higher tiers. Your files and workflows get locked into formats and clouds that are hard to leave, and the price keeps climbing because leaving is painful.
>
> It doesn't have to be that way. People all over the world build excellent tools and give them away, with the source open for anyone to check. Price Tag Zero collects the ones that replace the paid stuff, with no strings: no Pro tier, no trial, no subscription, no cloud upsell, nothing for sale. Ever.

> **The rules**
>
> 1. **Open source.** An OSI-approved license, with the code public.
> 2. **A real GUI.** A desktop app for Windows, macOS or Linux, or a web app you host yourself, with a release you can download. Command-line-only tools don't count.
> 3. **Nothing for sale.** No Pro tier, trial, subscription, paid add-on, paid cloud or hosting, enterprise edition or in-app ads.
> 4. **Donate buttons are fine** if they block nothing now and can't later.
> 5. **Active.** A commit or release in the last 12 months.
> 6. **Replaces something paid.** It does the main job of a well-known paid app.
>
> Every app here passes all six. The details, and the evidence each app needs, are in [the contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md#the-rules).

## Gaps

Some paid apps still have no free, open-source replacement that passes every rule. These are the big ones. Know an app that fills a gap, or a near miss that has changed? Please [suggest it](CONTRIBUTING.md#suggest-an-app). It's the most useful contribution there is.

- Pro Tools: professional multitrack recording, editing and mixing. Ardour comes closest, but its ready-to-run builds are sold.
- Sibelius: professional music notation. MuseScore Studio comes closest, but its maker sells sound libraries on the download page.
- VMware Workstation on Windows: full desktop virtual machines on Windows. VirtualBox's Extension Pack is sold for commercial use. Linux and macOS are covered (virt-manager, GNOME Boxes, UTM).
- Figma: collaborative interface design and prototyping. Penpot comes closest, but it sells hosted plans and an enterprise tier.
- Notion: an all-in-one workspace of docs, databases and tasks. AFFiNE, AppFlowy, Anytype and SiYuan all sell plans. The wikis and note apps listed here cover parts of it.
- VeraCrypt-style encryption: encrypted volumes and whole-disk encryption on Windows and macOS. VeraCrypt's license is not OSI-approved. zuluCrypt covers Linux, and Picocrypt-NG and SiriKali handle files and folders.
- Antivirus: a desktop antivirus with a real GUI. ClamTk, the best-known ClamAV front end, has gone inactive.
- Topaz Photo AI and Gigapixel: AI photo upscaling, sharpening and noise reduction. Upscayl comes closest, but it sells a cloud subscription.
- iZotope RX: audio repair, noise removal and stem separation. Ultimate Vocal Remover comes closest, but its repo has no LICENSE file.
- iStat Menus: menu-bar system monitoring on macOS. Stats comes closest, but a built-in module feeds its author's paid cloud dashboard.
- CleanMyMac: an all-in-one Mac cleaner, uninstaller and updater. Pearcleaner uses a Commons Clause license, which is not OSI-approved. GrandPerspective and Latest cover parts of it.

## Contributing

Suggestions are welcome, and every app is held to the same rules. Read the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) first, then [suggest an app with the issue form](https://github.com/RandyNorthrup/price-tag-zero/issues/new?template=add-app.yml) or open a pull request that edits `data/apps.yaml`. If a listed app starts selling something or goes quiet, [report it](https://github.com/RandyNorthrup/price-tag-zero/issues/new?template=report-app.yml). Wondering why a popular app is missing? See [Why isn't X here?](EXCLUDED.md). Looking for a replacement for one paid product? See [the A to Z table](REPLACES.md).

Please follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
